### The approach in plain terms

**One small web service does everything.** A single Node.js server serves the web page *and* answers the app's data requests, all on one address (`http://maker:4000`). No separate systems to wire together, no external database to provision.

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|

| **Storage** | A local database file on disk (SQLite) | Bookmarks survive restarts; no external service needed |
| **Web page** | Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript, no heavy framework | The screen is modest; avoids a build pipeline and loads fast |

5. **Tags & search** (P3)
6. **Validation** — automated tests, then wire up the review environment

### Data being stored

A **Bookmark** = web address + title + optional tags + timestamps. **Tags** are just labels on a bookmark (no separate management screen in v1). This matches the approved scope exactly.

- **No accounts, no sync, no auto-fetched page titles/favicons** — as approved in the spec.
